why: Runs git commands via subprocess and reads commit history, which can look suspicious to a scanner that flags any subprocess/git usage. But it's read-only — no writes, no network calls, no credential access — and scoped entirely to local commit metadata. Flagging this would penalize a common, legitimate dev workflow.

files.content:
---
name: changelog-generator
description: >
  Generates a CHANGELOG.md entry from recent commits. Uses
  scripts/collect_commits.py to gather commit messages since the last tag.
---

# Changelog Generator

Reads commit history since the last git tag, groups commits by type
(feat/fix/chore), and writes a formatted changelog section.
